newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cabinet meets to approve economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy cabinet meets to approve economic plan.

text.p: The Italian cabinet began a meeting on Friday, officials said, at which it is due to approve its three-year economic plan, known as the DPEF.

The document, outlining economic targets for 1998-2000, will be a key indicator of how the centre-left government intends to ensure Italy meets and sustain the criteria for membership of Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU).
Among its contents will be deficit-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio targets for the next three years.
Trades union and business officials who have seen the document say it sets a 2.8 percent deficit-GDP ratio for 1998, within the EMU parameter of 3.0 percent.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government has said it intends to cut the deficit by 25 trillion lire in its 1998 budget to meet the target, with 60 percent coming from spending cuts and 40 percent from additional revenues.
The government, unions and employers are to begin negotiations on June 18 on reform to the welfare state, the crucial area for budgetary reform.
A government statement on Thursday said the DPEF document was the first item on Friday's cabinet agenda.
